title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Sabotaging Electric Power Equipment

articles.content_en: Article 2: Where any person negligently damages electric power equipment, causing the serious consequences as stipulated in Article 1 of this Interpretation, the person shall, in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 119 of the Criminal Law, be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years for the crime of negligently damaging electric power equipment; if the circumstances are relatively minor, the person shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention.

Article 3: Where any person steals electric power equipment, endangering public security, but does not constitute the crime of theft, the person shall be convicted and punished for the crime of destroying electric power equipment; where the person's conduct simultaneously constitutes the crime of theft and the crime of destroying electric power equipment, the person shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provision of the Criminal Law that imposes a heavier punishment.
Where any person steals electric power equipment, without endangering public security, but criminal liability shall be investigated, the person may be dealt with according to the circumstances of the case as the crime of theft or other crimes.

Article 4: For the purpose of this Interpretation, "electric power equipment" means electric power equipment that is in operation, emergency use, or other use; electric power equipment that has been put into use with power supply but is temporarily suspended due to dry season, insufficient power, or other reasons; and electric power equipment that has been delivered for use but has not yet been connected to power supply. It does not include electric power equipment that has not been installed, or has been installed but not yet delivered for use.
The scope of calculation of direct economic losses in this Interpretation includes the amount of electricity loss, the costs of procurement, replacement, and repair of damaged equipment and materials, and direct economic losses caused to users due to power outages, among others.
